sentences.text:
_________
 Mr. Mandar Limaye a/w Mr. Vedant Bende for the Petitioners.
Ms. A.A. Nadkarni, Agp for Respondent/State.

__________
 Coram : Sandeep V. Marne, J.
Date : 4 September 2025.
P.C.:
1.

The Petition challenges order dated 2 August 2014 passed by Divisional Commissioner, Pune Division, rejecting the Application filed by the Petitioner under provisions of Section 48(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (the Act).

By that Application Petitioner had requested for withdrawal from acquisition proceedings and for return of land bearing Survey No.71/6, village Mundhwa, District Pune on the ground of failure on the part of the acquiring body to take possession thereof.
Since Petitioner's request for return of the land is rejected by the Divisional Commissioner by order dated 2 August 2014 the present Petition is filed.

Brief facts leading to the filing of the Petition are as under:

Petitioner claims to be the owner of land bearing Survey No.71/6, admeasuring 6 gunthas situated at village Mundhwa, District Pune.
It is claimed that said land came to be allotted to the share of the Petitioner by virtue of family partition.
By virtue of Notification issued under Section 4 of the Act, the land was acquired under urgency clause for the purpose of construction of railway siding by Bharat Forge Company.
The final Award was published on 27 October 1964.
The Petitioner claims that though the Award was published, possession of the land was never taken over nor was handed over to Bharat Forge Company.
Therefore, the Petitioner was advised to file an Application dated 2 May 2014 under provisions of Section 48(1) of the Act before the Collector seeking return of the land.

Since the Application was not decided,
Petitioner filed Writ Petition No.1085 of 2014, which came to be disposed on 1 April 2014 granting liberty to the Petitioner to make an Application under Section 48(1) of the Act before the Divisional Commissioner, who is the correct Authority to decide such Application.

Accordingly, Petitioner preferred Application dated 2 April 2014 before the Divisional Commissioner under Section 48(1) of the Act seeking exclusion of the land from Award dated 25 October 1964 and for return thereof.
By impugned order dated 2 August 2014, the Divisional Commissioner has proceeded to reject the Application preferred by the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.

Mr. Limaye, the learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner would submit that the Divisional Commissioner has proceeded to decide Petitioner's Application without grant of an opportunity of hearing to the Petitioner.
He would submit that hearing of the Application was scheduled on 2 June 2014 thereafter no date was fixed on account of which the Petitioner preferred Application dated 25 July 2014.
Instead of fixing the date of hearing, the Divisional Commissioner proceeded to reject the Application by order dated 2 August 2014.

The second grievance raised by Mr.
Limaye is about non-supply of various documents relied upon by the Divisional Commissioner for the purpose of inferring taking over possession of the land from the Petitioner.

He would submit that the Petitioner was not supplied with various notices and documents referred in the impugned order for the purpose of drawal of an inference that possession of the land was taken over from the Petitioner.
On the above two broad grounds, Mr. Limaye would pray for setting aside the order dated 2 August 2014 with a prayer for remand of the proceedings for decision afresh.

4. Ms. Nadkarni, the learned AGP appearing for the Respondents/State would submit that the impugned order has been passed by the Divisional Commissioner after grant of due opportunities of hearing to the Petitioner.
She would place on record roznama of proceedings conducted before the Divisional Commissioner.
She would submit that all the documents were k 4/9 8 wp 8721.15 as.doc duly supplied to the Petitioner and that the Petitioner has been duly heard before passing the order dated 2 August 2014.

She would submit that several documentary evidence would clearly reflect the factual position of handing over possession of the land in question to Bharat Forge Mr. Dnyanoba Dhondiba Pathare Through ... vs The Collector, Pune And Ors.

That Petitioner has requested for and accepted compensation in respect of the acquired land.
She would accordingly pray for dismissal of the Petition.
5. I have considered the submissions canvassed by the learned counsel appearing for rival parties.

6. So far as the first grievance of the Petitioner about non- grant of opportunity of hearing before passing the impugned order dated 2 August 2014 is concerned, the roznama placed on record shows that the Application was fixed for hearing on 2 June 2014 when the Petitioner and his Advocate were absent.
However, the Special Land Acquisition Officer No.17 was present.
The hearing was adjourned to 10 June 2014 when the Petitioner's Advocate was present.
It appears that on 2 June 2014 the Special Land Acquisition Officer No.17 submitted his written Reply.
On 10 June 2014 Respondent No.3-Bharat Forge Company Ltd. sought time to file Reply and the hearing was adjourned to 16 June 2014.
On 16 June 2014 the Petitioner's Advocate was present.
It appears that Respondent No.3 tendered its Reply.
The proceedings were kept for final hearing on 23 June k 5/9 8 wp 8721.15 as.doc 2014.
On 23 June 2014 Petitioner sought time to respond to the Reply filed by Respondent No.3.
Accordingly, the proceedings were adjourned to 25 June 2014.
The roznama indicates that on 25 June 2014 Petitioner canvassed his submissions in respect of Reply of Respondent No.3.
The proceedings were accordingly closed.
Ultimately, the Application came to be rejected by order dated 2 August 2014.

7. Perusal of the averments in the Petition would indicate that the Petitioner has suppressed the factum of fixation of dates of hearing of his Application on 10 June 2014, 16 June 2014, 23 June 2014 and 25 June 2014.

In paragraph 17 of the Petition a bald averment is made that the Petitioner was not present on 2 June 2014 but no hearing was granted nor any date was assigned by the Respondent No.4 on Application made by the Petitioner.

The relevant averments in paragraph 17 of the Petition read thus:
"17.

The Petitioner submits that the Petitioner was not present on 2nd June, 2014 before the Respondent No. 4, however, no hearing nor any date was assigned by the Respondent No. 4 on the Application made by the Petitioner.

The Petitioner submits that a reminder dated 25th July, 2014 was made to the Respondent No. 4 contending that the Hon'ble High Court had directed the Respondent No. 4 to decide the Application within 6 weeks from the receipt of the Application."
8.

The Petitioner thus has painted a false picture in the Petition as if no date of hearing was ever fixed by the Divisional Commissioner after 2 June 2014 when in fact Petitioner's k 6/9 8 wp 8721.15 as.doc Advocate appeared before the Divisional Commissioner on 10 June 2014, 16 June 2014, 23 June 2014 and 25 June 2014.

This Court does not appreciate the conduct on the part of the Petitioner in suppressing the material information and in attempting to mislead the Court to believe that the impugned order is passed without grant of any opportunity of hearing to the Petitioner.

In fact suppression of material information would be a fit ground for dismissing the Petition which is filed by invoking extra-ordinary jurisdiction of this Court under Article 227 of Constitution of India.

Be that as it may.
I am satisfied that the Petitioner was given due opportunity of hearing before passing order dated 2 August 2014.

9. Coming to the second grievance of the Petitioner about non-furnishing of documents by Divisional Commissioner before passing order dated 2 August 2014, I again do not find any substance in the said allegation.
Perusal of the impugned order dated 2 August 2014 would indicate that the Special Land Acquisition Officer No.17 had filed a Reply on 2 June 2014, which was apparently received by the Petitioner.
There is no allegation in the entire Petition that Special Land Acquisition Officer's Reply dated 2 June 2014 was not received by the Petitioner.
The entire documents which are relied upon by the Divisional Commissioner were apparently produced by the Special Land Acquisition Officer alongwith the Reply filed on 2 June 2014.

This is clear from the following observations in the impugned order dated 2 August 2014:
k 7/9 8 wp 8721.15 as.doc "

10. Since the Petitioner has not averred in the Petition that he has not received Reply filed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer No.17, the submission made on behalf of the Petitioner that the documents referred to in that Reply were not furnished to him
cannot be believed.

The record thus indicates that Petitioner was duly served with all the documents referred to in the Reply filed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer on 2 June 2014, Petitioner has canvassed his submissions before the Divisional Commissioner and has never complained about non- receipt of Reply filed by Special Land Acquisition Officer on 2 June 2014 or about non-furnishing of copies of documents referred in the said Reply.
Therefore, the second grievance of non-furnishing of documents is also misplaced.

So far as the merits of the case are concerned, the Divisional Commissioner has recorded a finding that though the Mutation Entry No.2411 does not reflect taking over possession of the land,
Shri Dyanoba Dhondiba Pathare had submitted Application dated 8 June 1968 admitting acquisition of the land admeasuring 6 gunthas in Survey No.71/6 for construction of Railway siding and had requested for payment of compensation of Rs.483/-.
The Divisional Commissioner has perused the compensation levy chart dated 18 June 1968 reflecting that the land owners accepted compensation of Rs.483/- on 5 August 1968.

Since a specific application was made by one of the Mr. Dnyanoba Dhondiba Pathare Through ... vs The Collector, Pune And Ors. on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195994133/
4 land owners that the land was acquired without payment of compensation and since request for compensation was made, it is unbelievable that possession of the land was not taken from the land owners.

Considering the above position, I do not find any valid ground to interfere in the impugned order.
The Petition is devoid of merits.
It is accordingly dismissed.
